English construction: Subject–verb agreement
Example: “The lantern glows. The lanterns glow.”
The verb changes with the singular or plural subject.

English construction: Existential there
Example: “There is a spare key in the drawer. There are two spare keys.”
There introduces the existence of something; the following noun phrase determines formal agreement here.

English construction: Passive with an agent
Example: “The mural was restored by three local artists.”
The patient becomes the grammatical subject; by introduces the agent.

English construction: Passive without an agent
Example: “The road was closed overnight.”
The construction can leave the agent unexpressed when the event or result matters more.

English construction: Get passive
Example: “The parcel got damaged in transit.”
Get plus a past participle is common in informal descriptions of events affecting something.
